# hive_a -- parallax background, made by tools/backgrounds/make_bg.py (do not edit by hand)
# hive_a: amber-lit cavern depths: a glowing core far away, organic ribbed columns in three depths
# (honeycomb, dripping resin with glowing drops), ceiling membranes. Columns run off the top and bottom of
# every layer and repeat outwards.
# layer<n> <parallax x> <parallax y> <y offset> [scroll px/s]
#   screen x of the layer = -camera_x * parallax_x (wrapped, the layer repeats horizontally)
#   screen y of the layer's top row = y offset + rise * parallax_y, where rise = how far the camera's top
#   is above its lowest position in the level (px, >= 0); so at the bottom of a level the layer's top
#   sits at the y offset and climbing moves the layers down
#   scroll: the layer's own drift in px/s (negative = to the left), added to its x
#   above / below a layer the engine repeats its first / last row (clamp to edge); for layer 0 these
#   rows are flat and equal to the fill colours
#   layer<n>_glow.png (when present): the layer's emissive pixels for bloom, same size
layer0 0.06 0.03 0
layer1 0.18 0.06 0
layer2 0.36 0.1 0
layer3 0.66 0.2 0
# fill <top r g b> <bottom r g b>: the colours above and below layer 0
fill 19 12 13 19 12 13
# fore <parallax x> <parallax y> <y offset>: fore.png (made by tools/backgrounds/fore.py), drawn IN FRONT of
# fore   the world, behind the HUD: dark silhouettes in its top 62 and bottom 52 rows, the middle empty but
# fore   for a thin pillar / chain / vine. x like a layer (-camera_x * parallax x, wrapped). y: keep it on the
# fore   screen -- its top row at the y offset on the 400 px view and 20 px higher on the 360 px view; use
# fore   parallax y only for a small bounded sway (the rise formula of the layers would carry the top band
# fore   into the middle of the screen); no clamp-to-edge rows above or below it.
fore 1.25 1.12 0
